rationale:
The supplied 9-step proof contains three independent analytic obligations. Each is a genuine, reusable lemma, and what is left over is a short assembly.
(i) sobolev_level_moment_factor: parent step 4, Simon's "trivial inequality" on p. 100: (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q_ε^{1/n}.
(ii) sobolev_level_energy_tonelli: parent steps 1–3 and 7. It is Tonelli on μ ⊗ dt⌞(0,∞), using ∫γ'(a−t)dt = γ(a) (FTC) and ∫1_{t<a}dt = a, and gives ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(P(t)+R(t)) dt ≤ ofReal(J).
(iii) sobolev_level_layer_cake: parent step 8, Simon 4.11 with α = n/(n−1) and t₀ = ε: ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal((t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_{t+ε})) dt = ofReal(((n−1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ).

How the children give the selected statement, by the supplied steps 5, 6 and 9:
- Step 5. For t > 0, multiply the hypothesis by (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} ≥ 0 and apply (i). This uses C ≥ 0 and P(t)+R(t) ≥ 0; the latter follows from integral_nonneg even for junk values.
- Step 6. Apply ofReal, integrate over (0,∞) with lintegral_mono_ae, and pull out the finite constant ofReal(C Q^{1/n}) with lintegral_const_mul'.
- Step 9. Bound the remaining integral by (ii), rewrite the left side by (iii), and return to ℝ with ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff, since C Q^{1/n} J ≥ 0.

subproblems.title: Moment factor: (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ (∫_{M_0}(h+ε)^{n/(n−1)} dμ)^{1/n}
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and ℓ ∈ ℕ, and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported, and let ε > 0 and t ≥ 0. Put p := n/(n − 1) and M_s := {x : h(x) > s}, and write μ(M_t) for the real measure μ.real(M_t). Then (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} · μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ (∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}. All powers are real powers (Real.rpow) of nonnegative bases, and ∫_{M_0} is the Bochner set integral.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ε t : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → 0 < ε → 0 ≤ t → (t + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) - 1)⁻¹ * (μ.real {x | t < h x}) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ (∫ x in {x | 0 < h x}, (h x + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂μ) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra. For A ⊆ E, μ[A] ∈ [0, ∞] is the measure of A and μ(A) = μ.real A is its real value (the toReal of μ[A]). ∫ denotes Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable integrands) and ∫⁻ lower Lebesgue integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is y ↦ max(y, 0), dt is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and x^y is the real power Real.rpow (used only with bases x ≥ 0). Source: step 4 of the parent proof (the 'trivial inequality' on the last page of the proof of Simon 5.7, p. 100), with the parts of parent steps 1 and 3 that it uses. Notation: p := n/(n − 1), K₀ := tsupport h, Q := ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ.

1. (Exponents.) As a real number n ≥ 2, so n > 0 and n − 1 > 0. Hence p = n/(n − 1) ≥ 0, 1/n ≥ 0, and p·(1/n) = (n/(n − 1))·(1/n) = 1/(n − 1). Also t + ε ≥ 0 because t ≥ 0 and ε > 0.
2. (Sets.) Since h is continuous, M_t and M_0 are open, hence Borel. If x ∈ M_t then h(x) > t ≥ 0, so x ∈ M_0; thus M_t ⊆ M_0. If x ∈ M_0 then h(x) ≠ 0, so x ∈ support h ⊆ K₀; thus M_t ⊆ M_0 ⊆ K₀. K₀ is compact because h has compact support, so μ[K₀] < ∞ (μ is finite on compact sets), and therefore μ[M_t] ≤ μ[K₀] < ∞.
3. (Integrability.) The function x ↦ (h(x) + ε)^p is continuous on E: h + ε is continuous and, because p ≥ 0, y ↦ y^p is continuous. It is ≥ 0 everywhere, since h + ε ≥ ε > 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg). A continuous function is integrable on a compact set for a measure that is finite on compact sets (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact). So (h + ε)^p is μ-integrable on K₀, and therefore on its subsets M_0 and M_t. The constant (t + ε)^p is integrable on M_t because μ[M_t] < ∞.
4. (Moment inequality.) Integrating a constant over a set of finite measure gives (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) = ∫_{M_t} (t + ε)^p dμ. For x ∈ M_t we have h(x) + ε > t + ε ≥ 0. Since y ↦ y^p is nondecreasing on [0, ∞) for p ≥ 0 (Real.rpow_le_rpow), (t + ε)^p ≤ (h(x) + ε)^p. Both functions are integrable on the measurable set M_t, so monotonicity of the set integral (setIntegral_mono_on) gives ∫_{M_t} (t + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^p dμ. Next, M_t ⊆ M_0 and (h + ε)^p is nonnegative and integrable on M_0, so monotonicity in the domain (setIntegral_mono_set) gives ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ = Q. Altogether (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) ≤ Q.
5. (n-th roots.) The left side of step 4 is ≥ 0, because (t + ε)^p ≥ 0 and μ(M_t) ≥ 0. Since y ↦ y^{1/n} is nondecreasing on [0, ∞) (1/n ≥ 0), ((t + ε)^p μ(M_t))^{1/n} ≤ Q^{1/n}. For x, y ≥ 0 we have (xy)^{1/n} = x^{1/n} y^{1/n} (Real.mul_rpow). Since t + ε ≥ 0, ((t + ε)^p)^{1/n} = (t + ε)^{p·(1/n)} = (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} by step 1 (Real.rpow_mul). Hence (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q^{1/n} = (∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_t ⊆ M_0 ⊆ tsupport h (compact), so μ[M_t] < ∞ and the continuous (h+ε)^p is integrable on M_0
Raise both nonnegative sides to the power 1/n; (xy)^{1/n} = x^{1/n}y^{1/n} and ((t+ε)^p)^{1/n} = (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)}

subproblems.title: Integrated truncation energy over levels: ∫_0^∞(∫γ'(h−t)D dμ + ∫_{M_t}K dμ) dt ≤ ∫(D + hK) dμ
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported. Let D, K: E → ℝ be nonnegative, with D μ-integrable and K μ-integrable on tsupport h. Let γ: ℝ → ℝ be C¹ and nondecreasing, with 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1 and γ = 0 on (−∞, 0]. Put γ' := deriv γ and M_t := {x : h(x) > t}. Then ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(∫ γ'(h − t) D dμ + ∫_{M_t} K dμ) dt ≤ ofReal(∫ (D + hK) dμ). Here ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral of a [0, ∞]-valued function with respect to Lebesgue measure dt, ofReal: ℝ → [0, ∞] is y ↦ max(y, 0), and ∫ denotes Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h D K : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ D x) → Integrable D μ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ K x) → IntegrableOn K (tsupport h) μ → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → Monotone γ → (∀ s, 0 ≤ γ s ∧ γ s ≤ 1) → (∀ s, s ≤ 0 → γ s = 0) → ∫⁻ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x, deriv γ (h x - t) * D x ∂μ) + ∫ x in {x | t < h x}, K x ∂μ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, (D x + h x * K x) ∂μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra. For A ⊆ E, μ[A] ∈ [0, ∞] is the measure of A and μ(A) = μ.real A is its real value (the toReal of μ[A]). ∫ denotes Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable integrands) and ∫⁻ lower Lebesgue integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is y ↦ max(y, 0), dt is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and x^y is the real power Real.rpow (used only with bases x ≥ 0). Source: steps 1, 2, 3 and 7 of the parent proof (integration over t ∈ (0, ∞) on the last page of the proof of Simon 5.7), for an arbitrary measure and abstract nonnegative data D, K. Notation: K₀ := tsupport h; P(t) := ∫ γ'(h − t) D dμ; R(t) := ∫_{M_t} K dμ.

1. (h and μ.) K₀ is compact (h has compact support) and closed, hence Borel. Off K₀ we have h = 0. For t ≥ 0, M_t ⊆ K₀, because x ∈ M_t gives h(x) > t ≥ 0, so h(x) ≠ 0. Each M_t is open (h is continuous), hence Borel. h is continuous with compact support, so it is bounded: |h| ≤ m for some real m. μ is σ-finite, being finite on compact sets in the σ-compact space E. So Tonelli's theorem applies to μ ⊗ (dt restricted to (0, ∞)).
2. (Truncated K.) Put K' := 1_{K₀}·K, which equals K on K₀ and 0 off K₀. K is integrable on the measurable set K₀, so K' is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff); also K' ≥ 0. Moreover hK' = hK everywhere: on K₀, K' = K, and off K₀, h = 0.
3. (γ'.) γ' is continuous (γ is C¹) and γ' ≥ 0 (γ is nondecreasing; Monotone.deriv_nonneg). For s < 0, γ vanishes on the open neighbourhood (−∞, 0) of s, so γ'(s) = 0. Two scalar identities hold for every a ≥ 0.
 (B1) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(γ'(a − t)) dt = ofReal(γ(a)). Split (0, ∞) into the disjoint measurable sets (0, a] and (a, ∞). On (a, ∞), a − t < 0, so the integrand is ofReal(0) = 0. On (0, a], t ↦ γ'(a − t) is continuous, hence integrable on (0, a] ⊆ [0, a], and it is nonnegative. So its lower integral there is ofReal(∫_0^a γ'(a − t) dt). Substitute s = a − t (intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_left): ∫_0^a γ'(a − t) dt = ∫_0^a γ'(s) ds. The fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub) applies, since γ is differentiable everywhere and γ' is continuous, hence interval integrable. It gives ∫_0^a γ'(s) ds = γ(a) − γ(0) = γ(a), because γ(0) = 0.
 (B2) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} 1_{t < a} dt = Lebesgue measure of (0, ∞) ∩ (−∞, a) = (0, a), which is ofReal(a − 0) = ofReal(a).
4. (One level.) Fix t > 0.
 (a) x ↦ γ'(h(x) − t) is continuous. It vanishes off K₀, because there h = 0 and γ'(−t) = 0 (−t < 0). So it is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some constant c. Since D is integrable, the product γ'(h − t)·D (bounded continuous times integrable) is μ-integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul). It is ≥ 0. So P(t) ≥ 0, and ofReal(P(t)) = ∫⁻ ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t) D(x)) dμ(x) = ∫⁻ ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t)) ofReal(D(x)) dμ(x). Here we use ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal for integrable nonnegative functions and ofReal(ab) = ofReal(a) ofReal(b) for a ≥ 0.
 (b) M_t is measurable and M_t ⊆ K₀, so K is integrable on M_t and R(t) ≥ 0. Then ofReal(R(t)) = ∫⁻_{M_t} ofReal(K) dμ = ∫⁻ 1_{M_t}(x) ofReal(K(x)) dμ(x) = ∫⁻ ofReal(K'(x)) 1_{t < h(x)} dμ(x). The last step holds because on M_t ⊆ K₀ we have K' = K, and off M_t both integrands are 0.
 (c) Put F(x, t) := ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t)) ofReal(D(x)) + ofReal(K'(x)) 1_{t < h(x)}. Since P(t), R(t) ≥ 0, ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) = ofReal(P(t)) + ofReal(R(t)) = ∫⁻ F(x, t) dμ(x). The lower integral is additive here because its first summand x ↦ ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t)) ofReal(D(x)) is a.e.-measurable (lintegral_add_left').
5. (Measurability on E × (0, ∞).) The following hold for μ ⊗ (dt restricted to (0, ∞)):
 - (x, t) ↦ ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t)) is measurable, since γ' and h are continuous.
 - (x, t) ↦ ofReal(D(x)) and (x, t) ↦ ofReal(K'(x)) are a.e.-measurable: D and K' are μ-integrable, hence a.e.-measurable, and a function of the first coordinate inherits this (AEMeasurable.comp_fst).
 - (x, t) ↦ 1_{t < h(x)} is the indicator of the measurable set {(x, t) : t < h(x)}.
 Hence F is a.e.-measurable on E × (0, ∞).
6. (Tonelli.) By step 4, the integrands ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) and ∫⁻ F(x, t) dμ(x) agree for every t ∈ (0, ∞). So ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) dt = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} (∫⁻ F(x, t) dμ(x)) dt. By Tonelli's theorem (lintegral_lintegral_swap; μ and dt are s-finite, and step 5 gives measurability) this equals ∫⁻ (∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F(x, t) dt) dμ(x).
7. (Inner integral.) Fix x ∈ E, so a := h(x) ≥ 0. The map t ↦ ofReal(γ'(a − t)) is measurable and the other factors are constant in t. Hence ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F(x, t) dt = (∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(γ'(a − t)) dt)·ofReal(D(x)) + ofReal(K'(x))·∫⁻_{(0,∞)} 1_{t < a} dt. By (B1) and (B2) this equals ofReal(γ(a)) ofReal(D(x)) + ofReal(K'(x)) ofReal(a). Since γ(a) ≤ 1, ofReal(γ(a)) ≤ 1. Since a ≥ 0, ofReal(K'(x)) ofReal(a) = ofReal(h(x) K'(x)). Therefore ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F(x, t) dt ≤ ofReal(D(x)) + ofReal(h(x) K'(x)).
8. (Outer integral.) By steps 6–7 and monotonicity of ∫⁻, ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) dt ≤ ∫⁻ [ofReal(D) + ofReal(hK')] dμ = ∫⁻ ofReal(D) dμ + ∫⁻ ofReal(hK') dμ. Additivity holds because ofReal∘D is a.e.-measurable. The function hK' is μ-integrable: K' is integrable, and h is continuous (so a.e.-strongly measurable) and bounded by m (Integrable.bdd_mul). Since hK' = hK (step 2), hK is μ-integrable too. D and hK are integrable and nonnegative, so ∫⁻ ofReal(D) dμ = ofReal(∫ D dμ) and ∫⁻ ofReal(hK') dμ = ofReal(∫ hK dμ). Finally ∫ D dμ ≥ 0 and ∫ hK dμ ≥ 0, so ofReal(∫ D dμ) + ofReal(∫ hK dμ) = ofReal(∫ D dμ + ∫ hK dμ) = ofReal(∫ (D + hK) dμ) by linearity of the Bochner integral (integral_add). This proves ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(∫ γ'(h − t) D dμ + ∫_{M_t} K dμ) dt ≤ ofReal(∫ (D + hK) dμ). ∎
proof_key_steps: K' := 1_{tsupport h}K is μ-integrable with hK' = hK; M_t ⊆ tsupport h for t ≥ 0; h bounded; μ σ-finite
γ' continuous, ≥ 0, zero on (−∞,0); (B1) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(γ'(a−t)) dt = ofReal(γ(a)) by substitution and FTC; (B2) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} 1_{t<a} dt = ofReal(a)
For t > 0: ofReal(P(t)+R(t)) = ∫⁻ [ofReal(γ'(h−t))ofReal(D) + ofReal(K')1_{t<h}] dμ, using integrability and nonnegativity of γ'(h−t)D and 1_{M_t}K
The integrand is a.e.-measurable on E × (0,∞); swap the integrals by Tonelli
Inner integral = ofReal(γ(h))ofReal(D) + ofReal(hK') ≤ ofReal(D) + ofReal(hK')
∫⁻ ofReal(D) + ∫⁻ ofReal(hK) = ofReal(∫D) + ofReal(∫hK) = ofReal(∫(D + hK)), since D and hK = hK' are integrable and nonnegative

subproblems.title: Shifted layer-cake identity (Simon 4.11 with α = n/(n−1), t₀ = ε)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and ℓ ∈ ℕ, and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported, and let ε > 0. Put p := n/(n − 1) and M_s := {x : h(x) > s}, and write μ(M_s) for the real measure μ.real(M_s). Then ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal((t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} · μ(M_{t+ε})) dt = ofReal(((n − 1)/n) · ∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ). Here ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral with respect to Lebesgue measure dt, ofReal y = max(y, 0) ∈ [0, ∞], powers are real powers of nonnegative bases, and ∫_{M_ε} is the Bochner set integral.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ε : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → 0 < ε → ∫⁻ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal ((t + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) - 1)⁻¹ * μ.real {x | t + ε < h x}) = ENNReal.ofReal (((n : ℝ) - 1) / n * ∫ x in {x | ε < h x}, (h x ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) - ε ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1))) ∂μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra. For A ⊆ E, μ[A] ∈ [0, ∞] is the measure of A and μ(A) = μ.real A is its real value (the toReal of μ[A]). ∫ denotes Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable integrands) and ∫⁻ lower Lebesgue integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is y ↦ max(y, 0), dt is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and x^y is the real power Real.rpow (used only with bases x ≥ 0). Source: step 8 of the parent proof (Simon 4.11 with α = n/(n − 1) and t₀ = ε, used on the last page of the proof of Simon 5.7), with the parts of parent steps 1 and 3 that it uses. Here the shift t ↦ t + ε is carried out inside the one-dimensional inner integral; this is equivalent to the parent's translation of the outer integral. Notation: b := 1/(n − 1), p := n/(n − 1), K₀ := tsupport h, f(x) := max(h(x) − ε, 0), g(t) := (t + ε)^b.

1. (Exponents.) As a real number n ≥ 2, so n − 1 > 0. Hence b > 0, p = n/(n − 1) = 1/(n − 1) + 1 = b + 1 > 0, and 1/p = (n − 1)/n.
2. (Sets.) Since h is continuous, each M_s is open, hence Borel. For s > 0, x ∈ M_s gives h(x) > s > 0, so x ∈ support h ⊆ K₀. K₀ is compact, so μ[M_s] ≤ μ[K₀] < ∞. Hence ofReal(μ(M_s)) = μ[M_s] for s > 0.
3. (Rewriting the integrand.) Fix t > 0. Then t + ε > 0, so g(t) = (t + ε)^b ≥ 0 and ofReal(g(t)·μ(M_{t+ε})) = ofReal(g(t))·ofReal(μ(M_{t+ε})) = ofReal(g(t))·μ[M_{t+ε}] by step 2. Moreover {x : t < f(x)} = M_{t+ε}: since t > 0, t < max(h(x) − ε, 0) holds iff t < h(x) − ε, i.e. iff t + ε < h(x). Therefore the left side equals L := ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ[{x : t < f(x)}]·ofReal(g(t)) dt.
4. (Tonelli / layer cake.) f is continuous, hence measurable, and f ≥ 0. g is continuous: Real.continuous_rpow_const with exponent b ≥ 0, and on [0, ∞) the base t + ε ≥ ε > 0. Hence g is integrable on every interval [0, T], and g ≥ 0 on (0, ∞). Write μ[{f > t}] = ∫⁻ 1_{t < f(x)} dμ(x). The function (x, t) ↦ 1_{t < f(x)} ofReal(g(t)) is measurable on E × ℝ, and μ is σ-finite (finite on compact sets in the σ-compact space E). So Tonelli's theorem gives L = ∫⁻ (∫⁻_{(0,∞)} 1_{t < f(x)} ofReal(g(t)) dt) dμ(x) = ∫⁻ (∫⁻_{(0, f(x))} ofReal(g(t)) dt) dμ(x). Since g is continuous and ≥ 0 on [0, f(x)], the inner lower integral is ofReal(∫_0^{f(x)} g(t) dt). Thus L = ∫⁻ ofReal(∫_0^{f(x)} g(t) dt) dμ(x). 5. (Inner integral.) Fix x. Substitute u = t + ε (intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_right) and apply the power rule for the exponent b > −1 (integral_rpow): ∫_0^{f(x)} (t + ε)^b dt = ∫_ε^{f(x)+ε} u^b du = ((f(x) + ε)^{b+1} − ε^{b+1})/(b + 1). If h(x) > ε, then f(x) + ε = h(x) and b + 1 = p, so this equals (h(x)^p − ε^p)/p = (1/p)(h(x)^p − ε^p). If h(x) ≤ ε, then f(x) = 0 and the integral over [0, 0] is 0. Hence ofReal(∫_0^{f(x)} g) = 1_{M_ε}(x)·ofReal((1/p)(h(x)^p − ε^p)) for every x.
6. (Restriction to M_ε.) M_ε is measurable, so by steps 3–5, L = ∫⁻ 1_{M_ε}(x) ofReal((1/p)(h(x)^p − ε^p)) dμ(x) = ∫⁻_{M_ε} ofReal((1/p)(h^p − ε^p)) dμ.
7. (Back to a Bochner integral.) x ↦ (1/p)(h(x)^p − ε^p) is continuous (p > 0), so it is integrable on the compact set K₀ ⊇ M_ε, hence on M_ε. On M_ε it is ≥ 0: there h(x) > ε > 0, and y ↦ y^p is nondecreasing on [0, ∞), so h(x)^p ≥ ε^p. For a function integrable and nonnegative on M_ε, the lower integral of ofReal of it equals ofReal of its integral. Hence L = ofReal(∫_{M_ε} (1/p)(h^p − ε^p) dμ) = ofReal((1/p)·∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ) = ofReal(((n − 1)/n)·∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ), using 1/p = (n − 1)/n from step 1. Together with step 3 this is the claimed identity. ∎
